subject: 99 Revere Beach Parkway Mixed-Use Rezoning
overview: The council approved a zoning change for 99 Revere Beach Parkway to allow mixed-use development and denied a $500,000 rate subsidy from water and sewer reserves. The meeting also included honors for a lifesaving rescue at a city pool and discussion of heavy truck traffic on residential streets.

items.title: High School Robotics Recognition
items.summary: The council congratulated the Medford Vocational Technical High School Robotics Team for their performance at the World ROV Championships.

items.title: Tufts Pool Lifesaving Commendations
items.summary: Councilors and the Fire Chief recognized recreation staff, lifeguards, and emergency responders for their successful team effort in saving a drowning youth.

items.title: Kiwanis Club Life Jacket Donation
items.summary: The council approved the donation of 50 life jackets from the Medford Kiwanis Club for use by the Recreation Department.

items.title: 100 Winchester Street Zoning Amendment
items.summary: A proposal for a 65-unit residential and commercial development was referred to the Community Development Board.

items.title: 99 Revere Beach Parkway Zoning Map Change
items.summary: The council approved rezoning this industrial parcel to a mixed-use district to facilitate transit-oriented residential development near the Wellington station. The 60-day public comment period was waived.

items.title: Tufts University Grant of Location
items.summary: The council approved underground utility work on College Avenue to connect athletic fields to an electrical power supply, subject to engineering conditions.

items.title: Route 16 Maintenance Request
items.summary: The council passed a resolution requesting that state agencies clean and mow overgrowth along Route 16 and near the Main Street Bridge.

items.title: School Property RV Parking Inquiry
items.summary: A resolution regarding a specific recreational vehicle parked on school grounds was placed on file following a response from the Superintendent clarifying the permit process.

items.title: Water and Sewer Enterprise Fund Subsidy
items.summary: A request to use $500,000 in retained earnings to subsidize water and sewer rates failed, with councilors arguing the funds are better used for critical infrastructure repairs. The funds will remain in the enterprise account.

items.title: Spring Street Heavy Truck Traffic
items.summary: A resident expressed concern over the regular use of residential Spring Street by oversized 18-wheeler trucks, resulting in property damage and noise.

items.title: Athletic Coaching Hiring Policy
items.summary: The council discussed the school department's implementation of a new committee-based process for hiring high school coaches.
